title: Git, integration-on-disk and artifact inventory adapters
description:
Objective: land the production enumerators for the Git/integration-on-disk class and the artifact object/staging class, registered into the recovery-inventory port registry. Slice 3 of 3 from task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a, split by architect-d46fcb95 on human direction 2026-08-09.

TWO hard dependencies, both real:
1. task-00956ac383784e81b0345bbf09256323 (Recovery-inventory contract and coverage protocol) - owns the class set, item shape, coverage proof, INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer and the port registry.
2. task-f6c9011b24634de7b22ad10a26579883 (Git ref and artifact object enumeration capabilities) - supplies the enumerators this slice calls, WHICH DO NOT EXIST TODAY.

*** WHY DEPENDENCY 2 EXISTS. Measured symbol by symbol at 2026-08-09 by architect-d46fcb95: GitObserver (packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts) declares exactly headCommit(), statusPorcelainV2(), lsFilesTracked(), lsFilesIgnored(), submodulePaths() - there is NO branch or ref enumeration, and grep for for-each-ref/show-ref/--branches/refs/heads over packages/runner/src returns ZERO. ArtifactStore declares exactly stageArtifact(), verifyArtifact(), deleteArtifact() and ArtifactFsPort has no directory listing - grep for readdir/listObjects/listStaging returns ZERO outside runtime-entrypoint.test.ts. The parent task's instruction to "reuse the hermetic Git observer and artifact store" is therefore not satisfiable as written; the capability is genuinely absent. Do NOT close that gap by reimplementing enumeration inside this module or inside a test - wait for task-f6c9011b. ***

MEASURED PRESENT: the hermetic Git boundary itself exists - packages/runner/src/scope/scope-git.ts (createNodeGitObserver, hermeticGitEnvironment, MAX_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_BYTES) with shell:false / bounded maxBuffer / timeout / windowsHide discipline - as does the artifact store (createArtifactStore, createNodeArtifactFs, verifyArtifact) over its <root>/objects/<sha256> layout. This slice composes those, extended by dependency 2.

Deliverable: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/git-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) and artifact-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) plus focused tests, each registering itself as a class enumerator through the contract slice's port registry.

NOT in scope: the contract, coverage protocol or aggregate (slice 1); provider/process/lock or workspace classes (slice 2); scheduler resource rows; adopt/quarantine decisions; project embargo; tests/fault.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/git-inventory.{ts,js}, artifact-inventory.{ts,js}, their focused tests, and the two-line registration edit in the slice-1 aggregate. This slice does NOT edit index.ts or index-surface.test.ts - slice 1 owns the root seam.

Consumer (global rail Clause 1): daemon coordinator task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: The Git/integration enumerator observes a real repository through the hermetic observer extended by task-f6c9011b, enumerating refs and the integration targets represented on disk, and binds every item to class, stable external identity, observed disposition facts and source proof digest; it never invokes git through a shell and never accepts a free-form command string.

The artifact enumerator lists objects and staging entries through the extended artifact store over its own <root>/objects/<sha256> layout and binds each item the same way; an entry whose name is not a valid content address is reported with a stable code rather than silently skipped.

An unavailable enumerator, a truncated or over-limit result, an absent repository or store root, and a missing negative proof each return RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER with truth UNKNOWN; an empty listing is never proof of absence and partial items never upgrade the class to COMPLETE.

Enumeration order and digest are deterministic across path separators and locale on Windows, macOS and Linux; duplicate external identities and entries outside the exact project or recovery window refuse rather than merge or drop.

Focused tests build real temporary Git repositories and real artifact-store bytes rather than a reimplemented fixture authority, assert each covered class generated at least one coverage case with a non-zero asserted count, pin the exact code and INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer on every refusal, and mutation-check that the coverage handling is reddenable.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0, with any residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded merge-base baseline.
taskRails: Do not start until task-f6c9011b24634de7b22ad10a26579883 has landed the ref and object enumeration capabilities. Closing that gap inside this module, or inside a test helper, is exactly the reimplementation the project rails forbid.

A configured class requires complete enumeration or a verifiable negative proof; an empty listing, an absent directory, and an unreadable entry are three different facts and must carry three different answers.
These are external-effect boundaries: never invoke git through a shell, never accept a free-form command string, and keep every child bounded by maxBuffer, timeout and windowsHide.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, and assert non-zero generated class coverage.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

SEAM CONFIRMED on disk: enumerator returns RecoveryInventoryPortReading (ENUMERATED{items,complete,negativeProofDigest} | UNAVAILABLE | UNSUPPORTED); collectRecoveryInventory (recovery-inventory.ts:206-246) maps it. Precedence measured in collectClass: throw->ENUMERATOR_FAILED, unreadable->RESULT_MALFORMED, UNAVAILABLE->ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED->CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, >4096->RESULT_OVER_LIMIT, !complete->RESULT_TRUNCATED, then admitItems (class/project/window/duplicate) and finally empty+null proof->NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING. Enumerator mints NO coverage code.

THREE-WAY MAPPING, decided and distinct per class.
GIT (via GitObserver.listRefs / headCommit / submodulePaths):
  empty listing on a readable repo -> ENUMERATED items[] complete:true negativeProofDigest=canonicalDigest(observation) -> COMPLETE
  absent repository (ScopeObserverError RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_FAILED, or listRefs undefined) -> UNAVAILABLE -> ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE
  unreadable record (RUNNER_SCOPE_STATUS_MALFORMED / _OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW) -> complete:false -> RESULT_TRUNCATED
  Unborn HEAD is NOT unreadable: listRefs succeeding already proved the repo observable, so headCommit failing with OBSERVATION_FAILED records head=null and stays COMPLETE.
ARTIFACT (via ArtifactStore.enumerateArtifacts -> enumerateArtifactsAt):
  empty objects dir -> COMPLETE with observationDigest as the negative proof
  RUNNER_ARTIFACT_MISSING (absent store root) -> UNAVAILABLE -> ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE
  RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED (unreadable listing/entry) -> complete:false -> RESULT_TRUNCATED
  RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE (port has no listDirectory) -> UNSUPPORTED -> CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED
  RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT (bad content address / non-FILE / digest mismatch) -> DoD 2 needs a STABLE CODE, and the PortReading union has no field for one. Both enumerators therefore return their own reading wrapper {reading, refusal} where refusal preserves the underlying code AND its layer verbatim (ARTIFACT_STORE vs ARTIFACT_FS_PORT, GIT_OBSERVER). The registration's enumerate returns only .reading, so the seam is unchanged. This is a pass-through of another slice's code, never a minted coverage code.

DETERMINISM: production normalises separators and sorts item identities and digest inputs with compareCodePoints from recovery-inventory-shape.ts. Drill 4 (localeCompare) is targeted at the GIT test, whose ref names are Zeta/alpha/base - codepoint orders Z<a<b, en-locale orders alpha<base<Zeta. Artifact names are lowercase hex + '.tmp' and cannot distinguish the two comparators, so that module asserts digest/order invariance under a reversed port listing instead. Recorded honestly rather than claiming a drill the fixture cannot kill.

DoD 5 requires REAL TEMPORARY GIT REPOSITORIES, not a reimplemented fixture authority. Build them under the OS temp root via mkdtemp — never inside the repo — and remove them in an afterEach that runs on failure, recursive and forced, since this host is win32. A stray .git fixture in a commit breaks the no-scratch-files rail.

Rail: NEVER invoke git through a shell and never accept a free-form command string. Drive the shipped hermetic observer; if a test needs a repository, create it through the same bounded mechanism the observer uses (maxBuffer, timeout, windowsHide all bounded).

Cases, each pinning the EXACT code and INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer:
  - Happy path: refs and on-disk integration targets enumerate to items bound to GIT_INTEGRATION_ON_DISK with stable external identity, observed disposition facts and sourceProofDigest.
  - listRefs ABSENT on the observer (it is optional) -> UNAVAILABLE, mapping to ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE. This is the case the optional signature makes reachable and it is easy to forget.
  - THE RAIL'S THREE-WAY DISTINCTION, which is the heart of this task: an EMPTY listing, an ABSENT repository, and an UNREADABLE entry are THREE DIFFERENT FACTS and must carry THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS. Assert each separately with its own code. Collapsing them is how "we looked and found nothing" later reads the same as "we could not look".
  - Empty listing with no negative proof -> NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING, never COMPLETE.
  - Over-ceiling -> RESULT_OVER_LIMIT; complete:false -> RESULT_TRUNCATED.
  - Duplicate external identity, and an entry outside the exact project or recovery window -> REFUSE rather than merge or drop.
Assert a non-zero generated case count for the class.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 5 MUTATION DRILLS — coverage handling that cannot go red proves nothing. Run each, confirm the NAMED case kills it, revert, confirm green before the next, and record the exact failing assertion.

  1. Return { status: "ENUMERATED", items: [], complete: true, negativeProofDigest: null } for an empty ref listing -> NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING must go RED. This is the "empty listing is not proof of absence" invariant.
  2. Silently skip an artifact entry whose name is not a valid content address -> the DoD 2 case must go RED. If it stays green the test is only counting valid entries and is blind to the drop.
  3. Collapse the empty / absent / unreadable answers into one code -> at least two of the three-way tests must go RED. If only one fails, the other two were never distinguishing anything.
  4. Replace the codepoint comparator with localeCompare -> the determinism test must go RED. If it stays green, the fixture is not exercising ordering and DoD 4 is unproven.
  5. Treat a missing observer.listRefs as an empty listing instead of UNAVAILABLE -> the optional-method case must go RED.
  6. Delete a .js bridge -> plain Node breaks while vitest stays green.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it is on disk — that happened to a file of mine earlier in this session. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof.

planningNotes.risks:
1. REBUILDING REF ENUMERATION VIA parseRefListing. The promotion note actively encourages it by asserting GitObserver has no ref method. It does — listRefs?() at scope-contract.ts:73. Re-parsing duplicates landed authority and is the rails' central prohibition.

2. TREATING A MISSING OPTIONAL METHOD AS AN EMPTY RESULT. listRefs and listDirectory are both optional. Undefined means "we could not look", not "there is nothing" — UNAVAILABLE, never an empty ENUMERATED.

3. COLLAPSING THE THREE-WAY DISTINCTION. The rail is explicit that an empty listing, an absent directory and an unreadable entry are three different facts needing three different answers. Merged, "we looked and found nothing" becomes indistinguishable from "we could not look" — the exact confusion the whole recovery-inventory protocol exists to prevent.

4. SILENTLY SKIPPING A BAD CONTENT ADDRESS. DoD 2 requires a stable code. A skipped entry is invisible in a green test, which is why drill 2 targets it specifically.

5. LOCALE-SENSITIVE ORDERING. localeCompare orders differently across machines and locales and would break DoD 4 only on someone else's box. Codepoint comparator, and normalise separators in production rather than in the test.

6. SHELLING OUT TO GIT. Forbidden by rail. Every child bounded by maxBuffer, timeout and windowsHide.

7. IN-REPO TEST ARTEFACTS. Real git repositories and artifact stores must be built under the OS temp root via mkdtemp and removed in an afterEach that runs on failure — recursive and forced, since this host is win32.

8. EDITING THE AGGREGATE OR SLICE 2. Both are DONE; touching either collides in the shared worktree.
